heading: CHAPTER XIV.
title: THAT WHICH CONCERNS A PRINCE ON THE SUBJECT OF THE ART OF WAR
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Chapter 14 turns from bad forms of military dependence to the prince's constant obligation to study war.
The argument divides peace-time preparation into action and study: drill, terrain knowledge, mental rehearsal, and historical imitation.
Neglect of arms loses states, while peace-time industry prepares the prince to resist fortune in adversity.
